title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinion on the Selection and Appointment of Technical Investigators in Intellectual Property Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Technical Investigation Officers in Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2017] No. 24

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

With the consent of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, the Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Technical Investigation Officers in Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation) are hereby issued to you for diligent implementation in light of practical work. If any problems arise during implementation, please promptly report them to the Supreme People's Court.

August 8, 2017

Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Technical Investigation Officers in Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation)

With a view to regulating the selection and appointment of technical investigation officers and strengthening the adjudication of technical intellectual property cases, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Servant Law of the PRC and the relevant provisions on the management of civil servants under employment system, taking into account the actual circumstances of intellectual property adjudication.

1. A technical investigation officer is a judicial auxiliary personnel responsible for investigating, inquiring, analyzing, and making judgments on technical issues involved in the adjudication of intellectual property cases, so as to provide professional technical opinions to judges in deciding cases.

2. Upon approval by the provincial civil servant competent department, an intellectual property court may, in accordance with the relevant provisions on the management of civil servants under employment system, employ technical investigation officers by contract.

Where required by the adjudication work, professional and technical personnel from patent administration and other departments who meet the qualification conditions may be seconded to intellectual property courts for exchange for a period of 1 to 2 years and serve as technical investigation officers during the exchange period. The exchange personnel from the patent administrative department serving as technical investigation officers shall be incumbent examiners.

Other professional and technical personnel who meet the qualification conditions for technical investigation officers may serve as part-time technical investigation officers upon recommendation by industry associations or relevant entities and review by the intellectual property court.

3. The selection and appointment of technical investigation officers shall adhere to the principle of the Party managing cadres, the principle of selecting persons with both integrity and ability with priority given to integrity, the principle of emphasizing actual performance, recognition within the industry, and pragmatism, and the principles of openness, equality, competition, and merit selection. It shall be carried out in accordance with the statutory authority, conditions, standards, and procedures, and shall highlight the professional characteristics of intellectual property adjudication.

4. Technical investigation officers are mainly selected and recruited from professional and technical personnel engaged in production, management, review, or research in fields such as machinery, chemical engineering, optics, materials, electronic information, computers, medicine, and biology.

5. To serve as a technical investigation officer, one must meet the following qualification conditions:

(1) Holding a bachelor's degree or above in a science or engineering major from a regular institution of higher education;

(2) Holding a professional technical qualification at the intermediate level or above;

(3) Having more than 5 years of work experience in production, management, review, or research in the relevant professional technical field.

In addition to meeting the above qualification conditions, individuals applying to serve as technical investigation officers shall also meet the conditions stipulated in the Civil Servant Law of the PRC.

6. A person shall not serve as a technical investigation officer under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Having been subjected to criminal punishment for a crime;

(2) Having been publicly expelled from public employment, or having had their employment or service contract terminated due to disciplinary or legal violations;

(3) Being under investigation for suspected disciplinary or legal violations and no conclusion has yet been reached;

(4) Being within a period of disciplinary sanction or the period of influence has not yet expired;

(5) Other circumstances that render the person unsuitable for serving as a technical investigation officer.

7. The procedures for appointing technical investigation officers by contract shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions on the management of civil servants under employment system.

8. An intellectual property court shall invite experts from relevant fields to jointly form a review committee to evaluate the professional level of candidates for technical investigation officers.

9. An intellectual property court and the technical investigation officer appointed by contract shall, on the principles of equality, voluntariness, and mutual agreement, sign a written employment contract specifying the rights and obligations of both parties. The employment contract shall include provisions on the contract term, position and job requirements, wages, benefits, insurance treatment, and liability for breach of contract. Upon mutual negotiation between the parties, the employment contract may be modified or terminated.

Upon the dissolution or termination of the employment contract, the intellectual property court shall issue a written certificate for the dissolution or termination of the employment contract. After completing the relevant procedures for the transfer of personnel files, social insurance relations, etc., as required, the appointed technical investigation officer shall no longer hold the status of a civil servant under employment system and shall be required to conduct the handover of official duties as stipulated.

The conclusion, modification, dissolution, or termination of an employment contract shall be reported to the competent department for civil servant management at the same level for record.

10. The term of an employment contract shall be 1 to 3 years. A probationary period may be stipulated in the employment contract, and the corresponding probationary period shall be 1 to 6 months.

The salary and benefits of appointed technical investigation officers shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions on the management of civil servants under employment system.

11. Persons serving as technical investigation officers through secondment for exchange or on a part-time basis shall not change their personnel and salary relations with their original units during their tenure as technical investigation officers.

12. An intellectual property court shall conduct an annual assessment of the performance of technical investigation officers in performing their duties and promptly adjust those who are incompetent or unable to continue performing their duties.

13. Other people's courts with jurisdiction over technical intellectual property cases may, after reporting to and obtaining the consent of the Supreme People's Court, select and appoint technical investigation officers by reference to these Opinions.

14. The interpretation of these Opinions rests with the Supreme People's Court.

15. These Opinions shall come into effect as of August 14, 2017.
